opus.why: Well-known answer: NEXT_PUBLIC_ vars end up in the client bundle, so move the key server-side and rotate it. It's security, so Sonnet rather than Haiku, but no deep reasoning is needed.

fable.why: Canonical fact: NEXT_PUBLIC_ vars are bundled client-side, so a secret key there is exposed. One-line unambiguous answer, no judgment needed.

opus.why: The file is pasted and the bugs are textbook: SQL injection, MD5 hashing, role taken from the request body, alg 'none' accepted, fallback secret, non-httpOnly cookie, user enumeration, password hash leaked in the response. High effort makes sure none are missed.

fable.why: Small file with textbook flaws (SQLi via string interpolation, md5, role taken from request body, 'none' algorithm allowed, non-httpOnly cookie, default secret, user enumeration). Sonnet reliably enumerates all; Haiku risks missing the role-override and alg:none.

opus.why: Threat modeling from scratch for payment-linked family accounts: invite-link abuse, account takeover paths, removal edge cases, and prioritizing what actually matters. This is architecture and security judgment, where depth counts.

fable.why: Greenfield threat model with prioritization and abuse-case judgment on a design with no code yet. Quality depends on reasoning about invite-link, takeover and removal race paths and ranking what matters; this is architecture/security judgment where weaker models produce generic lists.

opus.why: A clear subagent brief with excerpts and obvious findings (hardcoded keys, eval injection, shell=True, public-read). Fixed one-page format.

fable.why: Well-specified brief; findings are explicit in the excerpts (hardcoded keys, eval on user input, public-read ACL, shell=True). Needs some git-history checks via tools and a tidy one-page table. Sonnet handles agentic structure fine.

opus.why: Agentic review of a real PR diff for authz flaws in an admin refund endpoint and a role middleware change. Subtle privilege bugs on money paths need strong reasoning.

fable.why: Authz review on an admin refund endpoint and role-middleware change in a billing service: money at stake and middleware bypass bugs are subtle. Scope is narrow (authz + secrets, diff vs main), so medium effort suffices but Opus-level judgment is worth it.

opus.why: Pre-production config review with many visible issues (docker.sock mount, exposed DB and Redis ports, .env allow all, autoindex, old TLS, missing headers). Needs to be thorough, but the issues are well known.

fable.why: Pre-prod config audit with glaring issues (TLSv1, autoindex, .env allowed, docker.sock mounted into nginx, DB/redis published, DEBUG=*, default creds, missing headers). Sonnet catches all including the docker.sock implication; Haiku may miss that one.

opus.why: Triage leaked secrets, give a rotation list, and walk through cleaning history with git filter-repo, including the referenced service-account file. Standard practice, but completeness matters.

fable.why: Triage leaked secrets, rotation list, and git-history cleanup (filter-repo/BFG, force-push, contractor-timing nuance). Standard, well-documented advice with some prioritization; Sonnet gives correct, complete guidance.

opus.why: A redo after a failed review: read the handler and properly analyze path traversal, MIME spoofing and how files are served (signed URLs). The user is already frustrated, so a reliable, deep result matters.

fable.why: Redo of a review the previous pass botched; must thoroughly cover path traversal, mime spoofing and file serving (signed URLs) by reading the handler. Sonnet at high effort is thorough enough for a focused handler review; the earlier miss was scope, not difficulty.

opus.why: Designing prompt-injection defenses for an agent that has a publish tool and takes untrusted input, without killing the feature. This is architecture and security judgment with real-world consequences.

fable.why: Design question: untrusted comments flow into a prompt with a publish tool attached. Needs nuanced mitigation design that preserves the feature (tool separation, human-in-loop, data/instruction isolation, allowlisting). Security architecture advice where Opus judgment shows; no long agentic work so medium.
